judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 1 Indicators (same grade rank 0), so no rank-based developmental direction applies, and neither statement shows substantive expansion of the other. B1.2.7.2.3 (Reading / Sub-Strand 7: Comprehension, under 'Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand') asks learners to connect ideas and information in stories to their own experiences and world knowledge; B1.1.5.1.1 (Oral Language / Sub-Strand 4: Dramatisation and Role-Play, under 'Perform stories') asks learners to dramatise stories heard, with exemplars on identifying characters in a narrated story. The shared substance is genuine story engagement — both require holding and interpreting narrative content, one through personal connection while reading, the other through enacting a heard story — making them complementary story-comprehension experiences across different strands rather than one supporting success in the other. Evidence is mainly thin token overlap ('stories') plus a shared grade ancestor, which alone would not suffice; the pair-specific narrative-understanding coherence supports symmetric relatesTo only. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated with 24 omitted evidence items each, and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so absence of further linkage in the excerpts is not proof of absence.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain; resolved Grade coordinate rank 1 for each, gap 0), so developmental direction cannot come from rank and must be earned from text. B2.2.2.1 (Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand 2 Phonics) is 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write'; B2.4.10.1 (Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand 10 Narrative Writing) is 'Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the real or fictional world'. The phonics standard's own stated purpose includes writing, and the narrative standard is written composition at the same grade, giving substantive complementary coherence between encoding skill and composing connected text — useful instructional coherence rather than mere shared wording. However, the two statements share no capability that one visibly extends: one is sound–letter/blending mechanics, the other is communicative purpose and point of view, with no transcription or phonics language in the target. The 'phonics enables writing' inference is generic across all writing standards and is not pair-specific enough to support a same-rank buildsTowards claim, so the symmetric relatesTo judgment is taken with canonical endpoint order preserved and null direction. Nomination signals (shared BASIC 2 Grade ancestor at distance 3/3, weak 'b2' code-prefix, token jaccard 0.04 on 'and', trigram fragments 'con'/'rea'/'s a') are structural/lexical only and were disregarded as semantic evidence. Evidence limits: no Learning Components supplied for either endpoint; source evidence truncated for both (35 and 24 omitted items) with one source-ref excerpt itself truncated; upstream merge context applies to the BASIC 2 grade organizer and to B2.2.2.1 (CONT'D row merge), and those anomalies remain unresolved here.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same coordinate rank 1), so direction must rest on substantive text evidence rather than rank. B2.2.2.1 (Strand 2 Reading / Sub-Strand 2 Phonics) is 'Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write' — its stated purpose explicitly includes encoding for writing. B2.4.10.1 (Strand 4 Writing / Sub-Strand 10 Narrative Writing) requires learners to 'Narrate situations, express feelings and convey point of view about the real or fictional world', i.e. to compose connected written narrative text. Sound-letter correspondence and blending are the encoding proficiency that makes independent written narration feasible, so proficiency in the phonics standard supports likelihood of success in the narrative writing standard; the reverse support is not evidenced. This is a directional support claim, not a mandatory teaching sequence. Evidence limits: the nomination signals (shared BASIC 2 grade ancestor, weak 'b2' code-prefix and token/trigram overlap on stopword-like fragments) carry no semantic weight and were disregarded; both endpoints have no Learning Components supplied and truncated source evidence (35 and 24 omitted items), and one endpoint's source ref excerpt is itself truncated, so the composition/encoding link is inferred from the bounded statement text alone.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards under STRAND 4: WRITING (same rank 1, same statement-type grain). B2.4.3.1 (Sub-Strand 3: Writing Letters – Small and Capital) targets handwriting mechanics — using skills, strategies and knowledge of letter sounds/letters to write legibly and boldly. B2.4.7.2 (Sub-Strand 7: Controlled Writing) targets sentence-level construction — matching parts of sentences to composition, with source context showing re-arranging jumbled sentences logically. These are complementary writing competencies (transcription mechanics alongside logical sentence construction) that reinforce each other within the same grade's Writing strand, but the second standard's demand is logical/syntactic sequencing rather than an extension of legible letter formation, and at equal rank there is no substantive evidence that proficiency in one specifically enables success in the other. Token/trigram overlap was trivial ('of', 'to') and shared parents plus a weak 'b2.4' code prefix are not themselves semantic evidence, so a developmental direction is not asserted. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (35 and 24 omitted items), limiting confirmation of any explicit sequencing.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 3 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same canonical rank 2) under the merged 'Strand 2: Reading' organizer, but in different sub-strands: B3.2.7.2.1 sits under Sub-Strand 7 Comprehension / Content Standard B3.2.7.2 (use reading knowledge, skills and techniques to understand, interpret and appreciate literary texts) and targets understanding the purpose and features of poems, rhymes and fables; B3.2.9.1.1 sits under Sub-Strand 9 Fluency / Content Standard B3.2.9.1 ('Read texts fluently') and targets reading long texts with good pace, accuracy and expression. Same-rank developmental direction would need substantive evidence that is absent here, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.
